changes.index_pipeline.py: run() embeds at most max_batch_size (env SEARCH_INDEX_REFRESH_BATCH_SIZE, default 16) in chunks (SEARCH_INDEX_REFRESH_CHUNK_SIZE=4) and stops starting chunks after SEARCH_INDEX_REFRESH_TIME_BUDGET_SECONDS=15; checkpoint holds only really indexed ids; unprocessed ids stay out of the checkpoint so next call re-selects them; snapshot gains backlog_remaining; checkpoint indexed_at keeps microseconds so bounded batches are not re-selected by the >= last_indexed_at rule
changes.main.py: POST /api/search/index/refresh acquires the pipeline lock non-blocking: a concurrent call returns 200 {status: in_progress} immediately, never a second run; completed result adds status=completed, pipeline_snapshot shape unchanged (+backlog_remaining)
changes.scheduler_worker.py: assess_progress(); alive file touched only while progressing; unhealthy after SEARCH_INDEX_SCHEDULER_MAX_STALLED_TICKS (default 6) consecutive stalled ticks (in_progress or no-progress); log line carries progress reason, stalled_ticks, health; timeouts/HTTP errors remain failed ticks

reproduction: Before the change refresh_index ran pipeline.run unbounded under a blocking lock: a backlog > one tick made the 30s client time out while the server kept running and the next tick queued another run over the same unrecorded backlog (the old test_concurrent_refresh_callers... asserted runs==3). Equivalent to max_batch_size >= backlog.

tests.result: 224 passed, 25 skipped, 3 failed (test_zh_segmentation: jieba not installed in this venv, unrelated); qdrant_client missing so test_qdrant_backend ignored
new_tests: test_backlog_ten_times_batch_drains_with_no_double_embed (53 objects, batch 5, 11 calls, each embedded once, max_active==1)

note: Source-completion endpoint still waits on the lock (response needs a snapshot) but each run is now bounded.
